title: Suneil Anand, Son of Bollywood Legend Dev Anand, Dies at 70 in London
excerpt: The actor, director and custodian of the iconic Navketan Films banner suffered a heart attack in London on Saturday, ending a life intertwined with Indian cinema royalty.
body:
• Suneil Anand, 70, died of a heart attack in London on July 26, 2026. He was the only son of legendary actor Dev Anand and actress Kalpana Kartik.
  • Suneil managed Navketan Films, the production house founded by Dev Anand in 1949 that produced classics such as Guide, Jewel Thief and Hare Rama Hare Krishna.
  • He acted in four Bollywood films and directed Master (2001), one of India's earliest martial arts films, before working on the Hollywood-Indian crossover project Vagator Mixer.
  • His death in London mirrors his father's passing in the same city in December 2011 at the age of 88, also from a heart attack.

Suneil Anand, the actor, filmmaker and custodian of the storied Navketan Films production house, died of a heart attack in London on Saturday. He was 70. His niece, Gina Narang, confirmed the news to Indian media.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=j3FP1TgA1fw

Suneil was the only son of Dev Anand, one of Hindi cinema's most iconic leading men, and actress Kalpana Kartik. Born on June 30, 1956, in Zurich — while his parents were en route to the Karlovy Vary Film Festival — Suneil grew up straddling two worlds: the glamour of Bollywood and the cosmopolitan life his father cherished in London.

A Career in His Father's Shadow

Suneil's film career began with Anand Aur Anand in 1984, a father-son venture that failed to make a commercial impact. He followed it with Car Thief (1986) and Main Tere Liye (1988), but none achieved the success that defined his father's decades-long career. After earning a business administration degree from American University in Washington, D.C., and training in Wing Tsun martial arts in Hong Kong, Suneil channelled his interests into directing.

His directorial debut, Master (2001), was one of India's first attempts at a martial arts action film. While it drew modest attention, the project reflected Suneil's ambition to push Navketan into new territory. More recently, he had been developing Vagator Mixer, an English-language film set around Goa's famous beach culture, intended as a Hollywood crossover for the Navketan brand.

Guardian of the Navketan Legacy

If Suneil's screen career remained modest, his role as the keeper of Navketan Films gave him a different kind of significance in Indian cinema. Founded in 1949 by Dev Anand and his elder brother Chetan Anand, Navketan produced more than 35 films over six decades, including some of Hindi cinema's most enduring works: Guide (1965), Jewel Thief (1967), Hare Rama Hare Krishna (1971) and Johny Mera Naam (1970).

After Dev Anand's death at The Dorchester hotel in London on December 3, 2011 — also from a heart attack, at the age of 88 — Suneil took formal charge of the banner. It was Suneil who carried his father's coffin at the funeral service at Putney Vale Crematorium in London and later immersed his ashes in the Godavari river at Nashik.

A Family That Shaped Indian Cinema

The Anand family's contribution to Indian cinema extends well beyond Dev and Suneil. Dev's elder brother Chetan Anand won the Palme d'Or at the inaugural Cannes Film Festival in 1946 for Neecha Nagar. Younger brother Vijay Anand directed Guide and Jewel Thief. The family's extended connections include filmmaker Shekhar Kapur, adding another branch to one of Bollywood's most influential creative dynasties.

"He would like to go like a ripple flowing in the river."

— Dev Anand, from his autobiography Romancing With Life, reflecting on his own mortality

Diaspora Connections

Suneil spent much of his adult life between Mumbai and London, where a significant community of Indian entertainment figures and NRIs have long maintained ties. His death in the same city where his father passed away 15 years ago carries a poignant symmetry for the diaspora, many of whom grew up watching Dev Anand's films and associate the Anand family with a golden era of Indian cinema.

What's Next

The future of Navketan Films, which has not released a film since Dev Anand's Chargesheet in 2011, now falls into uncertainty. Suneil is survived by his sister Devina Anand. Funeral arrangements had not been publicly announced at the time of reporting. Tributes from across Bollywood are expected as the industry mourns the loss of the last direct link to one of its founding creative families.
